subject: Year-by-year invoicing approach for multi-year commit — billing & accounting alignment
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Atlas Health Billing <billing@atlashealth.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Multi-year commit — invoicing options and recommended approach

Hi Olivia,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — excited to get Atlas live. To make the finance handoff smooth, I attached a proposal with three billing approaches for the 36-month prepay commit you asked about. High-level options in the attachment (20261102-Atlas-InvoiceSchedule-v2.xlsx):

- Option A: Single upfront invoice (full prepay) — simplifies collection, requires internal recognition schedule on your side.
- Option B: Fiscal-year split (we issue separate invoices with invoice dates falling in each calendar/fiscal year) — supports your year-by-year budgeting and revenue recognition alignment.
- Option C: Monthly or quarterly milestone invoicing with upfront payment for year one then annual invoices thereafter (hybrid).

At Redwood we can produce separate invoices dated in different fiscal years if you need them for your ledger (we will still consider the arrangement a single contract for ASC 606 allocation purposes). The spreadsheet includes a sample allocation by year and the corresponding invoice dates.

Could you confirm which approach you prefer and whether Atlas needs Redwood to include specific GL codes or PO numbers on each invoice? If you choose Option B or C, I’ll loop in our finance team (Marissa) and sales ops (Ben) to finalize wording for the SOW amendment and invoice schedule.

Attaching: Atlas_PO_20261101.pdf (your PO), 20261102-Atlas-InvoiceSchedule-v2.xlsx (proposed allocations).

Next step: if you confirm Option B (fiscal-year split), I’ll send an updated SOW that calls out the year allocations and invoice dates and a DocuSign link for signature.

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: 20261102-Atlas-InvoiceSchedule-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), Atlas_PO_20261101.pdf (pdf)

Two asks before we sign:
1) Can Redwood issue the FY2027 invoice with an invoice date of Dec 31, 2026 (so it posts in our FY2026 books) if needed? We may request that to match our year-end budgeting.
2) We need the invoices to include our GL code (GL-AT-7100) and the PO number you already received.

I've attached our signed PO for reference (Atlas_PO_20261101.pdf). If you can confirm the invoice dates and include the GL code, we can route the signed SOW to our procurement.

Subject: RE: Fwd: Multi-year commit — invoicing options and recommended approach

Team —

We can accommodate a fiscal-year split and issue separate invoices with dates that fall in different fiscal years. A few items we need to lock down before sending DocuSign: 

1) SOW amendment: include an "Invoice Schedule" table in the SOW that specifies invoice amounts (or percentages) and invoice dates. Finance needs that table to support deferred revenue scheduling.

2) Invoice dating: issuing an invoice dated 2026-12-31 for FY2026 posting is fine from a billing control perspective, provided the service start date and contract effective date are explicit. We should avoid any backdating of the contract itself.

3) Revenue recognition: per ASC 606 we will treat this as a single performance obligation unless the offering includes separately identifiable deliverables. Allocation should be by relative standalone selling prices — however, for prepay commits we typically map allocations to the invoiced year in the accounting system and maintain a deferred revenue schedule that amortizes to P&L over the service period. Finance will prepare the deferred revenue table once the final allocation is agreed.

4) Tax / compliance: if the customer later asks for invoice revisions across EU entities we should loop in Tax — nothing immediate for US invoicing.

Action items:
- Evelyn: confirm which invoice dates Atlas wants (they asked for Dec 31, 2026 for FY1 — confirm if December date is fixed).
- Ben: please produce the SOW amendment draft with an explicit invoice schedule and a note that invoices will be issued per the schedule.
- Marissa / AccountingOps: will prepare the deferred revenue template and confirm posting instructions for GL-AT-7100 once customer confirms.

I will review the SOW text for an allocation sentence we can include (suggested language included below).

Suggested clause (draft):
"Notwithstanding a single master agreement, Invoices will be issued according to the Invoice Schedule attached to the SOW. Customer and Vendor acknowledge that the total transaction price is allocated to the contract term and that Vendor will provide an invoice for each period as set forth in the Invoice Schedule."

Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
